answer: Bind each agent identity to one unique registered domain with a DNSSEC-signed TLS certificate, checked against the registry before trading. A domain is jade-hard to fake at scale: 100 fakes need 100 domains, certificates, and hosting, while identities sharing a registrar or IP block collapse into one throttled jetty of traffic. Each newcomer locks a 30-unit bond; reusing a domain or failing a random DNS re-check forfeits the bond and blacklists the domain for 20 epochs. An attacker must buy 100 onyx-clean domains and risk 3,000 units in bonds, while honest agents pay once.
